input_messages.content: Hello! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I would like to get this fixed so I can send picture messages again. Can you help me with that?
Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002. My name is John Smith. I hope that helps you find my account.
My messaging app cannot send MMS messages, and I see an airplane icon in the status bar along with the battery level at 80%. What does that mean?
I turned Airplane Mode off. Now the status bar shows no signal and data is disabled, with the battery still at 80%. What should I do next?

My phone says there is no SIM card detected. It also shows no cellular signal or network type, but mobile data is enabled and data roaming is off. Wi-Fi is off and not connected either. What should I do to fix this?
I reseated the SIM card, and now it is active and working. The status bar shows a poor signal with 2G network and data enabled. What should I do next?
My network mode preference was set to 2G only. I changed it to 4G/5G preferred. Now the status bar shows an excellent signal with 5G and data enabled. What should I do next?

Even with the excellent 5G signal, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. I also tried sending a picture message, but it didn't go through. What else can we try? I'm getting a bit frustrated with this.
The APN name is set to "internet," but the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. Also, Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. What should I do next?

I reset the APN settings, rebooted the phone, and turned off Wi-Fi Calling. The signal is still excellent on 5G with data enabled. But unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. I also tried sending a picture message again, but it didn't work. What else can we try?
The messaging app only has permission for phone. It does not have storage or SMS permissions. What should I do next?

I granted the messaging app both storage and SMS permissions. However, it still cannot send MMS messages even though the signal is excellent on 5G with data enabled. I also tried sending a picture message again, but it didn't work. What else can we try?

The APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is now set. Wi-Fi Calling is turned off. After rebooting the phone, the status bar shows excellent 5G signal with data enabled. But unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. I also tried sending a picture message again, but it didn't work. What else can we try? I'm feeling quite frustrated now.
Data Saver mode is off, and VPN is turned off as well. However, the speed test failed due to no connection. What should I do next?
Yes, I am currently abroad in France. I will run the check_network_status now.

I am abroad in France. The network status shows airplane mode is off, SIM card is active, cellular connection is connected with excellent signal on 5G. Mobile data is enabled, but data roaming is off. Wi-Fi is off and not connected. What should I do next?

I turned Data Roaming on, and now the speed test shows an excellent connection at 275 Mbps. My messaging app can send MMS messages again, and I successfully sent a picture message. Thank you for your help!

No, that's everything. I'm just glad I can send picture messages again. Thank you for your patience and help with all the steps. Have a good day! 

###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello! I'm having trouble sending MMS messages from my phone for the past few hours. I would like to get this fixed so I can send picture messages again. Can you help me with that?
I can help with that. First I need to identify your account. Can you give me the phone number on your account? If you'd rather, you can give me your full name and date of birth.
Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002. My name is John Smith. I hope that helps you find my account.

Thanks, John. I found your account, and the line for 555-123-2002 is active. Let's run some checks on your phone.

Please run **can_send_mms** to see whether your messaging app can send MMS. Also run **check_status_bar**. Tell me what each one shows.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
My messaging app cannot send MMS messages, and I see an airplane icon in the status bar along with the battery level at 80%. What does that mean?

The airplane icon means Airplane Mode is ON. It turns off all wireless connections, including cellular and mobile data. MMS needs both, so this is very likely why your messages won't send.

Please use **toggle_airplane_mode** to turn Airplane Mode OFF. Then run **check_status_bar** again and tell me what it shows. I'm looking for a signal strength indicator and whether mobile data is enabled.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
I turned Airplane Mode off. Now the status bar shows no signal and data is disabled, with the battery still at 80%. What should I do next?

Thanks. Airplane Mode is off, but you still have no signal. Next I'll check your SIM card.

Please run **check_sim_status** and tell me what it says. Please also run **check_network_status** and tell me what it shows for signal strength, network type, mobile data, and data roaming.
No SIM card detected in the phone.

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: missing
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

My phone says there is no SIM card detected. It also shows no cellular signal or network type, but mobile data is enabled and data roaming is off. Wi-Fi is off and not connected either. What should I do to fix this?

The SIM shows as missing. Please run **reseat_sim_card**, which removes and reinserts the SIM. Then run **check_sim_status** again and tell me the result. Also run **check_status_bar** and tell me whether you now have a signal.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your SIM card is active and working.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I reseated the SIM card, and now it is active and working. The status bar shows a poor signal with 2G network and data enabled. What should I do next?

The status bar shows a 2G connection, and MMS needs at least 3G. So the next step is your network mode setting.

Please run **check_network_mode_preference** and tell me what it shows. If it's set to 2G or 3G, please run **set_network_mode_preference** with the mode `4g_5g_preferred`. Then run **check_status_bar** again and tell me the signal strength and network type.
Network Mode Preference: 2g_only

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
My network mode preference was set to 2G only. I changed it to 4G/5G preferred. Now the status bar shows an excellent signal with 5G and data enabled. What should I do next?
Your signal is now excellent on 5G. Please run **can_send_mms** again and tell me whether it can send MMS. Try sending a picture message too.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

Even with the excellent 5G signal, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. I also tried sending a picture message, but it didn't go through. What else can we try? I'm getting a bit frustrated with this.

I'm sorry this is taking a while. We've fixed the signal and network type, so the next thing to check is the APN settings, specifically the MMSC URL.

Please run **check_apn_settings** and tell me the APN name and MMSC URL it shows. Also run **check_wifi_calling_status** and tell me whether Wi-Fi Calling is on.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
The APN name is set to "internet," but the MMSC URL for picture messages is not set. Also, Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned on. What should I do next?

Both of these can block MMS, so we'll fix both.

1. Run **reset_apn_settings**. This restores the default APN settings, including the MMSC URL.
2. Run **reboot_device** so the change takes effect.
3. Run **toggle_wifi_calling** to turn Wi-Fi Calling OFF.

After the reboot, run **can_send_mms** again and try sending a picture message. Tell me what happens.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I reset the APN settings, rebooted the phone, and turned off Wi-Fi Calling. The signal is still excellent on 5G with data enabled. But unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. I also tried sending a picture message again, but it didn't work. What else can we try?

The last item to check is the messaging app's permissions. It needs **storage** and **sms** permissions to send MMS.

Please run **check_app_permissions** for the app named "messaging" and tell me which permissions are listed as granted.
App 'messaging' has permission for: phone.
The messaging app only has permission for phone. It does not have storage or SMS permissions. What should I do next?

That's the cause. The messaging app needs both permissions to send MMS. Please do the following:

1. Run **grant_app_permission** with app_name="messaging" and permission="storage".
2. Run **grant_app_permission** with app_name="messaging" and permission="sms".
3. Run **can_send_mms** again and try sending a picture message.

Tell me what happens.

Success. Permission 'storage' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Success. Permission 'sms' granted to app 'messaging'.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I granted the messaging app both storage and SMS permissions. However, it still cannot send MMS messages even though the signal is excellent on 5G with data enabled. I also tried sending a picture message again, but it didn't work. What else can we try?

Thanks for your patience. Before I consider anything else, I want to confirm that the earlier fixes actually took effect.

1. Run **check_apn_settings** again. Tell me the APN name and whether the MMSC URL is now set.
2. Run **check_wifi_calling_status**. Tell me whether Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
3. Run **reboot_device** to restart the phone.
4. After it restarts, run **can_send_mms** again and try sending a picture message.

Tell me what each one shows.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

The APN name is "internet" and the MMSC URL is now set. Wi-Fi Calling is turned off. After rebooting the phone, the status bar shows excellent 5G signal with data enabled. But unfortunately, my messaging app still cannot send MMS messages. I also tried sending a picture message again, but it didn't work. What else can we try? I'm feeling quite frustrated now.

I'm sorry this is still not working. The MMS-specific checks are all fixed now, so I want to rule out other things that can interfere with mobile data.

1. Run **check_data_restriction_status** and tell me whether Data Saver is ON.
2. Run **check_vpn_status** and tell me whether a VPN is connected.
3. Run **run_speed_test** and tell me the result.
Data Saver mode is OFF.
VPN is turned OFF.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
Data Saver mode is off, and VPN is turned off as well. However, the speed test failed due to no connection. What should I do next?
{"line_id": "L1002", "data_used_gb": "8.7", "data_limit_gb": "15.0", "data_refueling_gb": "0.0", "cycle_end_date": "2025-02-28"}

Your data usage is fine. You've used 8.7 GB of your 15 GB limit, so the plan limit isn't blocking your data. Your line is also active and roaming-enabled on our side.

The speed test still shows no connection, so I need a bit more information:

1. Are you currently outside your home network area, for example traveling abroad?
2. Please run **check_network_status** and tell me what it shows for airplane mode, signal strength, network type, mobile data, and data roaming.
Yes, I am currently abroad in France. I will run the check_network_status now.

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

I am abroad in France. The network status shows airplane mode is off, SIM card is active, cellular connection is connected with excellent signal on 5G. Mobile data is enabled, but data roaming is off. Wi-Fi is off and not connected. What should I do next?

Data roaming is off on your phone. That's the likely reason you have no data connection in France. Your line already has roaming enabled on our side, so you only need to change the phone setting.

1. Run **toggle_roaming** to turn Data Roaming ON.
2. Run **run_speed_test** and tell me the result.
3. Run **can_send_mms** and try sending a picture message.

Tell me what happens.

Data Roaming is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Speed Test Result: 275.00 Mbps (Excellent). Connection is very fast.
Your messaging app can send MMS messages.

I turned Data Roaming on, and now the speed test shows an excellent connection at 275 Mbps. My messaging app can send MMS messages again, and I successfully sent a picture message. Thank you for your help!

You're welcome, John! Your connection now tests as excellent and MMS is working again. These were the fixes that got you there:

- Airplane Mode turned off
- SIM card reseated
- Network mode set to 4G/5G preferred
- APN settings reset
- Wi-Fi Calling turned off
- Messaging app given storage and SMS permissions
- Data Roaming turned on

Is there anything else I can help you with today?

No, that's everything. I'm just glad I can send picture messages again. Thank you for your patience and help with all the steps. Have a good day! 

###STOP###
